about: Blanks a finished letter still has in it when it is about to leave the site: printed, or faxed to an insurance company.
One list for both sides. fighthealthinsurance/letter_placeholders.py reads it for the fax form on the server, and static/js/letter_placeholders.ts bundles it for the print and fax buttons.

Patterns are written in the part of regular expression syntax that Python's re (with re.ASCII) and JavaScript's RegExp read the same way: no lookbehind, no \s, no capturing groups. The only flag is i.

A Markdown reference link is never reported when the letter defines where it goes: [text][id], or [text][] where the text is the id, with a line of its own that starts [id]: https://. That definition is never reported either. Ids match whatever their capitals and spacing.
Text matched by an ignore pattern is never reported. Each placeholder pattern then claims what it matches, in order, so a later pattern never reports part of something an earlier one found.
A pattern here stops a fax, so each one is narrow on purpose: a citation like [1], a statute subsection like (a), an amount like $500 and a karyotype like 47,XXX all pass.

definition.name: where a reference link goes: [id]: https://... at the start of a line

link.name: a reference link: [text][id], or [text][] where the text is the id

ignore.name: a karyotype, which is a diagnosis rather than a blank
the brackets of quoting in legal writing
a single ordinary word in brackets, as a quotation adjusts its first word
examples: [We] ask the plan to cover it.
the policy says [the] member may appeal

ignore.name: a number masked down to its last four digits, as a statement prints it
a drug's package insert, however it is capitalised

placeholders.name: brackets that start with an instruction or a detail to fill in, not followed by a link
examples: [quote the specific reason given in the denial letter]

placeholders.name: brackets around a capitalised name, not followed by a link
brackets around a snake_case name, not followed by a link
brackets around a lower-case detail to fill in, not followed by a link
brackets around a choice of two or more pronouns, in any order
angle brackets that start with an instruction or a detail to fill in
angle brackets around a capitalised name
parentheses that start with an instruction
INSERT in capitals, followed by what to insert
a date written as its format
a number written in groups of Xs
the stand-ins the letter builder writes when it has no detail stored
